question: What do the visual-animation selector values mean, which of a weapon's settings sets applies when, and how do the multipliers combine?

selector: Field_c4814c93 is the zoom-level index. Each optic installs an aiming controller (Common/Gameplay/AimingControllers/WeaponsGadgets/Aim_*) whose zoom-level list uses the same member hash (Field_d96e9943) as the blueprint's list of settings objects. Entry 0 is always _ZoomLevels/DefaultBase (not aimed); entries 1 to N are the optic's Zoom_* levels.

Verified lists: {"Aim_Variable_4x00_1x00": ["DefaultBase", "Zoom_04x00_PiP", "Zoom_01x00_PiP"], "Aim_LPVO_4_6x00": ["DefaultBase", "Zoom_01x75_PiP", "Zoom_03x00_PiP", "Zoom_06x00_PiP", "Zoom_01x00_PiP"], "Aim_SVO_4_8x00": ["DefaultBase", "Zoom_04x00_PiP", "Zoom_06x00_PiP", "Zoom_08x00_PiP", "Zoom_02x00_PiP"]}. The optic files' multiplier selectors are exactly those indices: {"WPM_SCP_ElcanDR": [1, 2], "WPM_SCP_Tango6T": [1, 2, 3, 4]}.

From the trace only: counts match on 11 of 11 multi-level optics; -1 is used by state modifiers (mounted, bipod, buffer, global) and means any level, though whether it reaches level 0 is not established.
sets: Blueprint list entry 0 is the level-0 (hip) set and entry 1 the level-1 (aimed) set used with any optic.

The third set is installed by a replace-modifier on level 1 keyed to the iron-sights unlock (trace: 67 blueprints, registry label 'IRON SIGHTS ... WZL1'), so it applies when aiming with iron sights only. Replace-modifier selectors across the 70 blueprints: {"1": 72, "3": 1, "4": 1, "2": 1, "0": 2}.
stacking: No combine-mode field exists. The multiplier base class holds a priority, two booleans and registry links; every multiplier defaults to 1. The registry names the class '...CombinableModifierBase'.
WPM_Procedural_GlobalScaling_Primary is imported by 63 of 70 blueprints (not the sidearms).

Against plain multiplication (trace): identical values are restated where they would double-apply, for example the CDX40's inline 'Tango6T 60% Push/Kick on bolts' set beside the imported Tango6T file's own 0.6 on the same levels.

inference: Under multiplication of every active modifier, an aimed AK-205 or QBZ with the Mini Flex would run at 0.88 x 1.25 = 1.10 of its level-1 push and kick; if a level-specific entry replaces the generic one, 1.25. The 1.25 assumes the Mini Flex is the EotechEFLX riser variant, which was not confirmed.
A rifle with the SU-230 would run at 0.484 (multiplied) or 0.55 (replaced) on both of its levels.
unresolved: The combination rule (multiply all, or level-specific and higher-priority entries replace generic ones).
Whether selector -1 applies to level 0; the fallback set for levels 2 and above.
Field_7768ebf2 on the settings objects (59 / 55 / 28 to 35): not the gameplay field of view.

evidence.trace: Subagent trace of 24 November 2026 (scripts q1 to q19), spot-checked by verify.py.

leads.title: Visual firing animation: per-weapon push, kick, roll and settle values, optic multipliers and zoom-level selectors
leads.summary: Each weapon blueprint stores a 59-member per-shot animation struct per zoom level (hip, aimed, and an iron-sights aimed set), and Class_bfd4f199 modifiers scale its push and kick per zoom-level index of the fitted optic (Tango6T 0.6 on all four levels, SU-230 0.55 on both since 2.1.1.0, global primary scale 0.88 / 0.6); how multipliers combine is not established.
leads.reopenWhen: The combination rule is settled (the animation graph is read, or a recording compares sight motion with and without one multiplier), or a visual-recoil number is wanted on the site.
